title: Tenali Raman and the Spilled Pot of Ghee

keywords: tenali and the pot of ghee
full_text:
Tenali Raman’s cousin, a good-natured but notoriously lazy youth named Subbanna, had a bad habit of daydreaming extravagant fantasies instead of doing honest work.
One festival morning, Tenali gifted Subbanna a large earthenware pot filled with ten pounds of pure, fragrant cow's ghee, saying:
'Subbanna, carry this pot carefully to the market. Sell it for five silver coins, and use the money to buy seeds to plant your vegetable patch.'

Subbanna placed the heavy pot of ghee carefully upon his head, wrapped in a cloth ring, and began walking toward the bazaar.
As he walked down the dusty road, his mind began to spin an extravagant web of daydreaming:

'Ah!' thought Subbanna, smiling at the sky. 'I shall sell this ghee for five silver coins.
With the five silver coins, I will not buy common seeds; I will buy five pairs of fine hens!
The hens will lay hundreds of eggs, which will hatch into thousands of chickens!
I shall sell the chickens and buy ten she-goats!
The goats will multiply into a herd of a hundred!
I shall sell the goats and buy twenty fine milk cows!
I will become the wealthiest dairy lord in Vijayanagara!
I will build a three-story mansion with fountains of rosewater!
I will marry the wealthiest merchant’s daughter, and when she asks me to fetch water from the well, I will turn to her with supreme aristocratic disdain, shake my head proudly, and shout:
"NO! NOT AT ALL!"'

Lost completely in his imaginary glory, Subbanna made a violent, haughty gesture, shaking his head violently from side to side!
*CRASH!*

The heavy earthenware pot slipped from his head, slammed onto the hard cobblestones, and shattered into a hundred jagged fragments!
The ten pounds of rich, golden ghee spilled across the dirt road, soaking into the dust, where stray dogs and crows immediately descended to feast!

Subbanna sat on the roadside stones, clutching his empty head, weeping bitterly:
'Woe is me! My chickens are gone! My goats have vanished! My cows have died! My three-story mansion is ruined!'

Tenali Raman, who was walking behind, tapped him on the shoulder with his walking cane:
'Subbanna, dry your tears. Your chickens and cows were never born, and your mansion was built of smoke.
He who builds castles in the clouds trips over the stones of reality. Get up, take this broom, sweep the road, and earn a real copper with your hands. For a single real drop of milk earned by honest toil is worth ten thousand imaginary oceans of ghee!'

Subbanna learned the lesson of mindfulness, abandoned his idle fantasies, and learned to focus his mind upon the reality before him.
moral: Building imaginary castles in the air while neglecting the task at hand leads to the loss of real blessings.
